findings.evidence: ComplexSpinDensity.lean:370 `lemma isParityInvariant_re_iff {ρ : SpinDensityC} (h : ρ.IsTimeReversalInvariant)`; line 303 `lemma ofReal_h1_re {ρ : SpinDensityC} (h : ρ.transversity.im = 0)` uses the weaker hypothesis for the same reality fact; Positivity.lean:226 `IsParityInvariant` is the two diagonal equalities, and the complex predicate adds only `ρ.mat idxMM idxPP = ρ.mat idxPP idxMM`, which under `ρ.posSemidef.1.apply idxPP idxMM` is `conj t = t`.
findings.fix: State the unconditional characterisation `isParityInvariant_iff : ρ.IsParityInvariant ↔ PDF.IsParityInvariant ρ.re ∧ ρ.transversity.im = 0` (its two halves are `IsParityInvariant.re` and `IsParityInvariant.im_transversity`), or at least weaken the hypothesis to `(h : ρ.transversity.im = 0)` as `ofReal_h1_re` already does; derive the current time-reversal form from `IsTimeReversalInvariant.im_transversity` if still wanted, and fix the docstring at line 237.
findings.issue: `isParityInvariant_re_iff` assumes `ρ.IsTimeReversalInvariant` (every entry real), but the converse `PDF.IsParityInvariant ρ.re → ρ.IsParityInvariant` only needs `ρ.transversity.im = 0`: the diagonal is already real (`coe_re_mat_apply_self`), and hermiticity gives `ρ.mat idxMM idxPP = conj (ρ.mat idxPP idxMM)` (the `hconj` in `IsParityInvariant.im_transversity`), so the double-flip relation is exactly reality of transversity. The docstring of `IsParityInvariant.re` (lines 237–239) states the false claim that the converse "needs time-reversal invariance".

summary: The matrix-level bounds sit at the RCLike level with the real lemma a specialisation, and the SpinDensityC/SpinDensity maps carry the hypotheses they need, except one: the parity transfer back from the real part is stated under full time-reversal invariance when only reality of the double-flip entry is used.
